methods.name: Stage-Progression

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Climate & Energy (found 0 same-stage, 2 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 9 same-sector peers exist in Climate & Energy, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Svante, a Series E climate and energy technology company founded by Brett Henkel, has raised $318M to date. The broader Climate & Energy sector includes nine peer companies, comprising one public comparable (Linzatech, ticker LNZA) and eight private peers including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen. However, the peer-median approach was not applicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within narrow valuation bands—only two adjacent-stage peers were identified where at least three datapoints are required for reliable triangulation.

The stage-progression method was the sole applicable approach. Using total capital raised of $318M as a valuation proxy and applying a typical 1.4x step-up multiplier for the Series E to next-stage transition yields an implied valuation of $445M.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $378M (low) to $512M (high), with a median of $445M. Key uncertainties include the absence of direct peer-median anchoring in Svante's narrow valuation tier and stage cohort, which limits confidence in the multiplier itself. The single-method triangulation also leaves the valuation sensitive to assumptions about typical Series E step-up dynamics in climate tech. Resolution of these uncertainties would require either identification of additional same-stage comparables with disclosed valuations or access to transaction-level data from recent Series E or growth-stage rounds in the sector.
